correctness.rationale: At diag(a,-b), differentiating the positive spectral projector multiplies an off-diagonal entry by 1/(a+b), so differentiation of the positive eigenvalue times that projector gives the Hermitian Schur mask (1,q;q,0). The 2-norm is one by the entrywise formula and the first diagonal coordinate. Independently optimize in trace norm: the Hermitian trace unit ball is the convex hull of signed rank-one orthogonal projectors. A unit projector with first diagonal r has output trace norm squared r^2+4q^2 r(1-r), using the nonpositive determinant. On [0,1] this has maximum 1 at r=1 up through q^2=1/2, and otherwise maximum 4q^4/(4q^2-1) at r=2q^2/(4q^2-1). Trace duality and mask symmetry transfer the maximum to operator norm. The exhibited real symmetry has unit input and top output eigenvalue (t+sqrt(4q^2+(1-4q^2)t^2))/2, attaining the maximum at t=1 or t=1/sqrt(4q^2-1), as appropriate. The threshold is a/b>1+sqrt(2) in the stated infinitesimal sense. For global bounds the nonzero determinant polynomial yields finitely many crossings on a segment, with derivative bounds integrated between them; the identically singular segment is rank at most one, with its positive part either the input or zero according to affine trace, and bounded on both pieces. The profile increases on its upper branch to 2/sqrt(3); derivative ratios first at fixed indefinite input then as b/a->0 approach this ceiling. Frobenius sharpness already occurs in the positive cone. The claims apply on the real space of Hermitian matrices, not automatically to unrestricted perturbations. The inspected check.py gives finite corroboration only; 1892 checks is the frozen report, not a fresh run.
